text:
maya: Quick thought — propose a "pilot slit-fence" rollout pattern: slice traffic by tenant, ramp inside each slice, and have an automatic hard fallback that sends a tenant back to the previous variant on either latency or error spikes. Keeps blast radius small and avoids global flapping.

ajay: sounds promising. main worry is KV cache warmup + session affinity. if we flip mid-session we could get bad tail latency because caches miss.

sam: can we do session affinity with a TTL so active sessions aren't moved during the ramp? e.g. session-affinity: 10m.

liz: also need signal smoothing. raw 1-min P95 bounce will cause churn. debounce and evaluation windows matter. i'd lean toward p95 over 5m + error rate over 5m and a 2m debounce.

nora: where do we evaluate the thresholds? router-level (fast) or central controller (global signal)? tradeoffs: router is low-latency but sees only local load; controller sees global but slower.

ajay: hybrid — router enforces immediate hard SLO (if local p95 > threshold then short-circuit) and controller reconciles aggregate metrics and does the official slice flip. router flip should be reversible quickly, controller flip persists policy.

maya: agreed. sample config sketch:
```yaml
pilot:
  slices: 128
  slice_policy: "tenant_id % slices"
  rollout:
    initial_pct: 1
    max_pct: 25
    step_sec: 900
  session_affinity_ttl_sec: 600
  fallback:
    latency_p95_ms: 300
    error_rate_pct: 1.5
    evaluation_window_sec: 300
    debounce_sec: 120
  router_guard:
    local_latency_p95_ms: 450
    local_error_rate_pct: 5.0
```


liz: nice. one more: quotas and golden traffic. we should keep a reserved pool (2-5%) that never goes to the pilot variant so we have a clean baseline to compare.

sam: yes — golden traffic helps differential signals and regression detection. also thought: if cache warmup is a problem, mark slices as "warmup-required" and only increase traffic after a successful warmup probe.

maya: warmup probe idea is good. define a probe path that exercises KV access pattern and short sequences. probe success => slice marked warm.

nora: need to handle multi-variant sessions where a single user request fans out to multiple model variants (reranking + generator). the router should tag requests so replay/trace can attribute to variants.

ajay: implementation note: avoid storing per-tenant state in router; use token in header for affinity + a small LRU for recent flips. router should be mostly stateless. controller writes target percentages to config store; routers poll.

maya: quick ops commands for emergencies: `/pilot pause <pilot-id>` to freeze, `/pilot rollback <pilot-id>` to force revert slices to previous variant, `/pilot promote <pilot-id>` to promote and drain old variant. add audit log.

deploy-bot: deployment maya/pilot-slitfence -> model-v6 started: slices=128 initial=1% :rocket:

liz: runbook note — when router-local guard trips for >3 consecutive windows, ops pager. add rate-limited alerts to avoid alert storms.

sam: test plan: unit tests for router decision logic, integration tests with fake latency/error injection, e2e with staged warmups and golden traffic checks.

maya: follow-up: i'll draft an RFC with the config shape, router vs controller responsibilities, metrics to collect (per-slice p95, error_rate, cache_miss_rate, probe_success), and a runbook. owner: maya. deadline: next Tue.

nora: +1, cc @platform for rollout automation hooks.

ajay: one more micro concern — telemetry cardinality. per-slice per-tenant metrics could explode. suggest rollup: emit per-slice aggregates and sample per-tenant traces only when anomalous.

liz: agreed. keep metrics light but keep linkable traces.

maya: ok — onboarding checklist: 1) RFC, 2) router guard PR, 3) controller reconcile PR, 4) runbook, 5) canary job. i'll ping infra and observability.

maya: thanks all — quick sync next week to finalize thresholds. :thumbsup:
